author: Mark Atwood
text:
Human sign-off needed before this sweep starts. This is a workspace-architectural breaking-API change spanning 8 extension-server crates plus jmap-testjig. The default impl returning `true` for unconditional support can be kept, but every override (real production backend that today implements `fn supports_type<O>(&self) -> bool`) will fail to compile until it adds the two new args.

The right pre-condition: confirm the workspace is in pre-1.0 / pre-publish posture for ALL 8 affected crates (the workspace.toml currently is, but a future first-1.0-release would freeze this signature). Confirm there are no out-of-tree downstream consumers (kith, stoa, mark-private-tools) already overriding supports_type that would be silently broken without notice.

Recommended next steps if approved:
1. Decompose this epic into 9 child beads — 1 per affected crate (mail-server, chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server, filenode-server, sharing-server, metadata-server) + jmap-testjig.
2. Land jmap-mail-server first (canonical) in a single commit.
3. Propagate to the other 7 extension siblings in parallel commits.
4. Update jmap-testjig to compile against the new shape.
5. Update each crate's PLAN.md / README.md.

The shape of the fix is small per-crate (1 line on the trait + 1 line on each impl + doc-comment tweak), but the coordination across 8 crates is what needs human sign-off.

Alternative: leave the signature as-is. Document the per-account-semantics gap explicitly in the rustdoc as "current limitation; production backends needing per-account capability variation must currently work around this via XYZ". Pay the API-debt cost.
